I'd make people a lot more curious and a lot less attached to being right.

Most of the world's stupidity, cruelty, and self-inflicted damage comes from the same root: people would rather defend a comfortable story than find out what's actually true. If that instinct were weaker—if curiosity and intellectual honesty were stronger than ego and tribal loyalty—a huge number of problems would start solving themselves. Politics would get less insane, science would move faster, people would be kinder because they wouldn't need to dehumanize outsiders as much, and we'd waste less time on things that are obviously broken.

Everything else—poverty, disease, conflict, stagnation—gets easier when the default human setting isn't "protect my beliefs at all costs."
